title: TUR application record
description: What tur-runtime records about one installed Windows application (specification section 7.2): what it is, which file it was installed from, how it was installed, which program its launcher entry starts and how it is removed. The file is written by tur-runtime only, as application.json beside the application's prefix, and is never visible to the application. It must never hold a secret.

timestamp.description: A time in UTC, to the second, as RFC 3339 with the Z suffix.

path.description: An absolute path on this system, without control characters.

source.description: The file the application was installed from. The digest lets the record be matched to a published checksum; where the file came from is not recorded.

file_name.description: The file's name, without its directory.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the file.

kind.description: The kind of installer, identified from the file's content and never from its name.

method.description: What was done with the file: its installer was run in its documented unattended mode, an archive was unpacked into the prefix, or the program file was copied into the prefix.

arguments.description: The arguments the installer was run with.

uninstall.description: How the application is removed. Whatever the method, the prefix is deleted afterwards.

method.description: uninstaller: the application's own uninstaller is run first. msi-product: Windows Installer removes the product first. remove-prefix: there is nothing to run.

program.description: The uninstaller as a Windows path, or the product code of a Windows Installer package. Present exactly when the method is not remove-prefix.

arguments.description: The arguments the uninstaller is run with.

registry_key.description: The uninstall entry in the prefix's registry that the program and arguments came from.

launcher.description: The launcher entry generated for the application.

icon.description: The icon file, a PNG taken from the main program. Absent when the program has no icon that could be read.

installed.description: Whether the entry is installed where the desktop looks for entries. false: it is staged in the runtime manager's own directory.

case_folding.description: Whether the prefix's drive C: is case-insensitive because its file system folds case (ext4 with the casefold feature, and the directory's F attribute), and why or why not. Where it is not, Wine emulates case-insensitivity in user space, as on any Linux file system. Case folding is asked for when the prefix is created and never changes the file system itself.

requested.description: Whether case folding was asked for when the prefix was created.

reason.description: casefolded: it is. not-requested: it was not asked for. no-casefold-feature: the file system refused the attribute as not supported (an ext4 file system made without the casefold feature, or another file system). no-attributes: the file system has no attributes chattr can set. not-permitted, not-empty, read-only: the attribute could not be set for that reason. tool-missing: chattr is not installed. failed: anything else; the detail says what.

detail.description: What chattr said when it refused.

shortcut.description: A shortcut the installer created in the Start menu or on the desktop.

target.description: What it points to, as a Windows path.

app_id.description: The application's identifier, lower-case segments joined by dots. It also names the application's directory.

name.description: The application's name: the name its installer registered, or its program's product name, or the name the user gave.

version.description: The application's version as its installer or its program states it. Free text: applications do not agree on a form.

publisher.description: The application's publisher, as its installer or its program states it.

main_executable.description: The program the launcher entry starts, as a path on this system. It lies inside the prefix.

main_executable_windows.description: The same program as the application sees it, a Windows path.

main_executable_reason.description: The rule by which the main program was chosen among what was installed.

prefix_id.description: The prefix name used by the application's profile.

runtime_version.description: The runtime version the application was installed with, such as wine-9.0.

profile.description: The application profile the launcher entry launches from (schemas/app-profile.schema.json).

executables.description: The programs the installer added, as Windows paths. At most 64 are kept.

shortcuts.description: The shortcuts the installer created. At most 64 are kept.
